headline: Advance Daily Vehicle Permits for Beach and Trail Access
reservation: Daily vehicle permits can be reserved up to five days in advance and are highly recommended for weekend visits during peak summer months. Camping reservations are handled via the Ontario Parks website and often reach capacity months ahead for July and August. Always check the official Ontario Parks portal for current permit availability and potential swimming advisories.

days.title: Oak Savanna and Dunescape

stops.name: Oak Savanna Trail
stops.detail: Walk through one of the largest remaining oak savanna ecosystems in North America.

stops.name: Pinery Dunes
stops.detail: Ascend the boardwalks to view the fragile dune systems and Lake Huron's expanse.

days.driving: Allow 15–25 minutes; traffic may slow near park gates.
days.note: Stay on marked boardwalks to prevent erosion of the sensitive dune grass.

days.title: Riverside Paddling and Forest Vistas

stops.name: Old Ausable Channel
stops.detail: Paddle a canoe or kayak through this calm, sheltered waterway to spot turtles and herons.

stops.name: Carolynian Forest Trail
stops.detail: Explore the diverse flora characteristic of this southern Ontario ecological zone.

days.driving: Allow 10–20 minutes; local cycling is a viable alternative.
days.note: Water levels in the channel are generally stable but check for seasonal weed growth.

days.title: Lake Huron Shoreline Exploration
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Beach 9
stops.detail: Relax on the sandy shores and observe the unique coastal geology of the region.

stops.name: Heritage Trail
stops.detail: Learn about the park's history and the formation of the Ausable River system.

days.driving: Allow 15–30 minutes; parking fills early near popular beach access points.
days.note: Swimming conditions are subject to Lake Huron currents and water quality tests.

intel.title: Beach Access Parking
intel.text: Lots at popular beaches like Beach 1 and 2 fill rapidly on sunny weekends. Utilize the shuttle if available or arrive before mid-morning to secure a spot.

intel.title: Reliable Shoreline Signal
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally stable throughout the park due to the proximity to Grand Bend. Some interior wooded trails may experience minor interference.

intel.title: Grand Bend Amenities
intel.text: Full services including fuel and groceries are located in Grand Bend, just north of the park. There are no fueling stations within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Day-Use Peak Hours
intel.text: Park entry gates can experience significant queues between 10 AM and 2 PM on weekends. Weekday visits offer a more tranquil experience for trail walking.

intel.title: Advance Vehicle Permits
intel.text: Reserve your daily vehicle permit online before traveling to ensure entry during busy periods. Permits are verified at the gatehouse or through automated kiosks.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at London International (YXU) and drive north; stop in Grand Bend for beach supplies and food before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger cars are ideal for the paved park roads; bicycles are highly recommended for navigating between beaches and campsites.
plan.goldenHour: The Lake Huron shoreline, particularly Beach 1, is renowned for sunsets throughout the summer and autumn months.
